events.title: IntelliJ IDEA released
events.summary: JetBrains shipped IntelliJ IDEA in January 2001 — a Java IDE with deep code navigation, refactoring, and static analysis built in.
events.about: IntelliJ IDEA popularized smart autocomplete, safe rename, and extract-method refactors in Java before competitors caught up. It grew into a platform for Kotlin, Android Studio, and plugin ecosystems spanning Python, Go, and Rust. Teams still benchmark other IDEs against its refactoring and find-usages accuracy.

narrative.whyChosen: IntelliJ IDEA set the bar for IDE intelligence and influenced every major editor since.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved developers would pay for tooling that understands code structure, not just text.
narrative.problemSolved: Early Java IDEs were glorified text editors; large codebases needed automated navigation and safe refactors.

events.title: Wikipedia launched
events.summary: Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger launched Wikipedia on January 15, 2001 — a collaboratively edited encyclopedia that became developers' default reference.
events.about: Wikipedia is the overview source cited across Techline events — and the daily starting point for programmers researching APIs, history, and standards. Its wiki model influenced internal company wikis and Ward Cunningham's original wiki concept.

narrative.whyChosen: Wikipedia became the universal free reference for technical and historical facts.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved large-scale collaborative knowledge curation could work.
narrative.problemSolved: Authoritative encyclopedias were expensive, slow to update, and incomplete on tech topics.

events.title: Drupal 1.0 released
events.summary: Dries Buytaert released Drupal 1.0 on January 15, 2001 — open-sourcing the drop.org community software as a modular CMS.
events.about: Drupal is a PHP CMS for complex sites — content types, views, roles, and thousands of modules for government, university, and enterprise portals. Drupal 8+ rebuilt on Symfony components; today it powers large multilingual and accessibility-focused sites that outgrow simpler blogging tools.

narrative.whyChosen: Drupal pioneered modular, community-governed CMS architecture for ambitious web projects.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed how open-source CMSs could serve enterprises and institutions, not just blogs.
narrative.problemSolved: drop.org experimenters wanted to extend the software themselves instead of waiting for one maintainer.
